topics.label: Course welcome and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the lecture series on cancer etiology, and sets the learning objectives.

topics.label: Endogenous, genetic, and environmental determinants of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining the relative contributions of intrinsic cellular mutations, genetic predispositions, environmental exposures, stochastic factors, and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and viral mechanisms of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents and oncogenic viruses contribute to cancer development through cell cycle deregulation, immunosuppression, and chromosomal translocations.

topics.label: Aflatoxin metabolism and DNA adduct formation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how the dietary fungal toxin aflatoxin is metabolically converted by liver oxidases into a reactive epoxide that forms mutagenic DNA adducts.

topics.label: UV radiation and pyrimidine dimer formation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical mechanism by which ultraviolet radiation directly induces thymine dimers and leads to mutations when repair systems are overwhelmed.

topics.label: Chemical carcinogens, xenobiotic metabolism, and tissue specificity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how chemical carcinogens such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and aromatic amines undergo xenobiotic processing to induce DNA transversions, oxidative stress, or organ-specific malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and the two-stage carcinogenesis model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms of tumor promoters, illustrating how agents like asbestos and phorbol esters drive clonal expansion through chronic inflammation and intracellular signaling without directly mutating DNA.

topics.label: Host developmental timing and tissue susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how developmental windows, tissue proliferation states, and hormonal environments influence cellular susceptibility to carcinogenic transformation.

topics.label: Mutational signature analysis in cancer genomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines how high-throughput genomic sequencing identifies distinct mutational signatures that correlate with specific historical carcinogen exposures.

topics.label: Epidemiological cohorts, urinary biomarkers, and biobanks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses human population-level methods for identifying carcinogen exposure using large-scale biobanks and urinary metabolite biomarkers.

topics.label: In vivo animal testing for carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the utility, protocols, and limitations of whole-animal rodent models in assessing chemical toxicity and carcinogenesis.

topics.label: In vitro mutagenicity testing and the Ames test
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the bacterial Ames assay for evaluating mutagenic potential and discusses the strengths and limitations of cell-based in vitro screening.

topics.label: Carcinogen risk-benefit analysis and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by evaluating the trade-offs between carcinogen exposure and practical benefits while summarizing the core principles of environmental carcinogenesis.
